papers.summary: Affective variability is a pervasive phenomenon with important implications for cognition, behavior, and well-being. Yet the broad concept of variability may conflate distinct processes, such as transient fluctuations versus more sustained shifts. papers.title: Robotic surgery in gastrointestinal emergency settings: A systematic review
papers.summary: BACKGROUND Robotic-assisted surgery has become an established component of elective minimally invasive surgery, yet its role in emergency gastrointestinal surgery remains uncertain. Emergency procedures pose unique challenges, including time-critical decision-making, complex anatomy, and limited opportunities for extensive preoperative planning. AIM To evaluate the current evidence regarding the feasibility, safety, and clinical outcomes of robotic surgery in the emergency gastrointestinal setting. papers.title: Universal Basic Capital: A Review of Economic Implications of Robotized Wealth Distribution
papers.summary: Automation, artificial intelligence, and robotics are reshaping the structure of the global economy. While these technologies raise productivity, they also concentrate returns among the owners of automated capital and widen the gap between labour income and capital income. Universal Basic Capital (UBC) is a redistributive model in which a share of the wealth generated by robots and AI is pooled and paid out to every citizen, most commonly as a periodic dividend. papers.title: A robotic neck exoskeleton for children with poor head control: a feasibility study
papers.summary: The ability to properly orient the head is essential for learning motor and cognitive skills in child development. Children with severe motor disabilities often struggle to hold their head upright and move it in a controlled manner. Existing solutions, such as passive head equipment and physical therapy, are limited and insufficient. We recently developed a robotic neck exoskeleton to support the head and control its three-dimensional movements. papers.summary: The algorithms developed for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) are often challenging to test on actual vessels due to high operational costs and safety considerations. papers.title: Contextual Bandits and Optimistically Universal Learning
papers.summary: We consider the contextual bandit problem in general action and context spaces. This generalizes the standard multiarmed bandit to the case where side information is available—for example, patients’ records or customers’ history—which allows for personalized treatment. We focus on consistency (vanishing regret compared with optimal policy) and show that for large classes of non-independent and identically distributed (non-i.i.d.) contexts, consistency can be achieved regardless of the reward mechanism, a property known as universal consistency.
